title: MEGATRON setup wizard — answers file
description:
The non-interactive input to `megatron install --config answers.yml`, and the file the interactive TUI writes out so that a manual install becomes a reproducible one (ARCHITECTURE.md 6.2b, issue #5).

THE GOVERNING IDEA: an insecure install is not something this file validates against, it is something this file CANNOT EXPRESS.

ARCHITECTURE.md 6.2b promises 'there is no path through the wizard that produces an insecure install', as the structural answer to MagnusBilling's default root/magnus. A schema that merely rejects weak passwords would still be a schema with a password field in it — and every field in a config file eventually gets filled in with something bad, committed to a repo, and copied between deployments. So there is no password field anywhere in this document, at any nesting level, and `additionalProperties: false` everywhere means one cannot be added by an operator who wants one. Credentials are generated by the wizard and written to a mode-0600 secrets file; they are never an input.

A useful consequence, and the reason operators will actually adopt this: the answers file contains no secrets, so it is safe to commit to the operator's own configuration repository. Reproducible installs stop being in tension with keeping credentials out of git.

The same principle is applied to every other setting where a wrong value is a security incident rather than a preference — the admin bind address is an enum of loopback forms rather than a string, so 0.0.0.0 cannot be typed; SIP over UDP cannot be enabled without restricting it to allowlisted trunks; and the prepaid/postpaid fail direction has no default, because ARCHITECTURE.md 4.4 says it must never be chosen by accident.

STATUS: contract design. The Go installer does not exist (issue #5) and cannot be built on the machine this was written on (no Go toolchain). This document has been checked with jsonschema 4.26.0, and ci/check_wizard_answers.py proves that each insecure variant below is rejected — that is the only claim made for it.

version.description: Schema version this file targets. Present so `megatron upgrade` can migrate an older answers file rather than guessing.

profile.description: `shield` is the wedge: MEGATRON in front of an operator's existing switch, relaying clean traffic to it. It is first in the list because it is the deployment that requires no migration and no risk to their running platform, and it is how most operators will meet this product.

hostname.description: Fully-qualified name this node answers to. Required even in shield mode: TLS certificates are issued against it, and an operator who cannot name their switch cannot be given a certificate.
hostname.$comment: Pattern rather than `format: hostname`, for the reason given on network.public_ipv4 — and a fully-qualified one, because a bare label cannot have a certificate issued against it.

node_id.description: Stable identifier for this node in telemetry and the blocklist. Generated if absent.

public_ipv4.description: The address the world reaches this node on. `detect` asks the wizard to determine it from outside, which is the case that matters: a switch behind an unnoticed NAT is the single biggest source of 'it doesn't work' in this industry, and the operator usually does not know it is happening.
public_ipv4.$comment: A pattern, not `format: ipv4`. JSON Schema treats `format` as an annotation by default — a validator that has not been handed a format checker silently accepts anything. ci/check_wizard_answers.py does enable one, but a constraint that depends on how the caller configured their validator is not a constraint, and this file is the thing the Go installer will be written against.

behind_nat.description: Set only when the operator knows better than the preflight. The wizard detects this and will refuse to proceed on a contradiction rather than quietly build a switch whose SDP advertises an unroutable address.

sip.description: Transports. TLS is mandatory and is not a checkbox: a spoofed-source flood cannot complete a TLS or TCP handshake, so connection-oriented SIP is structurally immune to the entire spoofed-source attack class (edge/README.md). Pricing TLS as the default and UDP as the constrained exception is policy, not tuning.

oneOf.description: Let's Encrypt. The wizard provisions and renews.
Operator-supplied. PATHS ONLY — the key never appears in this file, which is what keeps the file committable.

udp.description: Plain UDP on 5060. Carriers still require it, so it cannot simply be banned — but it can be made impossible to leave open to the internet. `restrict_to_trunks` has no `false` case: enabling UDP means enabling it for an allowlist.

trunks.description: Carrier source prefixes permitted to speak UDP to this node. Must be non-empty: an empty allowlist that still opens the port is the worst of both.

admin.description:
The admin console and the telemetry API.

NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT: there is no username, no password, no API key and no token. The wizard generates them and writes them to a mode-0600 file, then prints a one-time recovery code. That is the whole of the structural answer to CVE-era MagnusBilling defaults — you cannot ship root/magnus if the file cannot say `magnus`.

bind.description: An enum, not a string, so `0.0.0.0` cannot be typed. Operators reach the console over an SSH tunnel or the authenticated reverse proxy — the same rule the telemetry contract applies to the node agent.

reverse_proxy.description: Optional authenticated proxy in front of the console. Note there is no `tls: false`: a proxy that terminates plaintext would undo the bind restriction it exists to relax.

fail_direction.description: What happens to a call when the authorizer is unreachable. Deliberately NOT uniform, and deliberately without defaults: ARCHITECTURE.md 4.4 says this must be explicit in configuration and must never happen by accident. Rejecting a prepaid call loses one call; allowing it can lose unbounded money to a fraudster. Refusing a credit-checked postpaid customer's traffic during our own outage is worse than billing them slightly late.

currency.description: ISO 4217. Money is stored as integer micro-units regardless (ci/policy_check.py, MONEY-NOT-FLOAT); this only affects presentation.

magnus_import.description: Migration as a wizard step rather than a separate manual chore. Paths only — a database password is not an input here either; the wizard reads a dump the operator has already produced.

mode.description: `shadow` rates traffic in parallel without billing it, so an operator can compare MEGATRON's figures against their existing switch before trusting it. It is the default because asking an operator to cut over on faith is how this product does not get adopted.

Matches ShieldMode in contracts/shield-telemetry.openapi.yaml. `monitor` classifies and reports but blocks nothing — it is how a cautious operator starts, and how the shield proves its false-positive rate on their real traffic before it is trusted to drop anything.

upstream.description: Required in transparent mode: the operator's existing switch, which clean traffic is relayed to.

reputation_feed.description: The opt-in fleet-wide threat feed. Default off and explicitly opt-in, because it is the one setting here that sends anything off the operator's box. Only attacker addresses and signatures are shared, never customer data — a position taken now, while it is still free.

then.$comment: Transparent mode with nowhere to relay to is a black hole that silently drops every legitimate call, which would look exactly like a successful shield.

verification.description: The wizard ends by placing a real call and confirming media flowed, so the operator's first experience is proof it works rather than a login screen and a hope (ARCHITECTURE.md 6.2b).

destination.description: E.164. A number the operator controls and can watch ring.

require_media.description: Signalling success alone is not success. A call that sets up and carries no audio is one of the three money-losing failure modes this platform exists to design out, and the install-day check is where that habit starts.

allOf.$comment: UDP without an allowlist is unrepresentable at the object level, but UDP must also never be the ONLY transport reachable: TLS is always provisioned above, so this only guards the shape.
